# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 56

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 12

---

## Disagreement 1 — 56:2 "sacred spirit" vs. "holy spirit" vs. "Holy Spirit"

- **EMET:** "the sacred spirit who dwelt in the flesh"
- **LOGOS:** "the holy spirit who dwelt in the flesh"
- **PNEUMA:** "the Holy Spirit who dwelt in the flesh"
- **Greek:** *to pneuma to hagion* — the holy spirit
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the Holy Spirit who dwelt in the flesh." *Hagion* = holy/sacred; "holy" is the standard English translation; "sacred" (EMET) is an unusual choice for this established divine title.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 56:2 "served this spirit well" vs. "served the Spirit well"

- **EMET:** "his flesh served this spirit well"
- **LOGOS:** "his flesh served this spirit well"
- **PNEUMA:** "that flesh served the Spirit well"
- **Note:** All three agree on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "his flesh served this Spirit well." The demonstrative "this" helps track the referents in a complex sentence.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 56:2 "walked in holiness and purity, in no way defiling"

- **EMET:** "walked in holiness and purity, in no way defiling the spirit"
- **LOGOS:** "walking in holiness and purity, not defiling the Spirit in any way"
- **PNEUMA:** "walking in holiness and purity, never defiling the Spirit at all"
- **Note:** Stylistic variation only.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "walking in holiness and purity, not defiling the Spirit in any way" (LOGOS). "In any way" preserves the absolute nature of the non-defilement.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 56:3 "labored together with the spirit" — all agree substantially

- **EMET:** "labored together with the spirit and cooperated with it"
- **LOGOS:** "labored together with the spirit and cooperated with it"
- **PNEUMA:** "laboring alongside the Spirit, cooperating with it"
- **Note:** Agreement on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "labored together with the Spirit and cooperated with it." The doublet preserves Hermas's emphasis.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 56:3 "valor and courage" vs. "valor and fortitude"

- **EMET:** "conducting itself with valor and courage"
- **LOGOS:** "conducting itself with valor and fortitude"
- **PNEUMA:** "with bravery and strength"
- **Greek:** *andreiotēs kai tolma* — manliness/valor and daring/boldness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "conducting itself with valor and fortitude" (LOGOS). *Andreiotēs* = manly valor/courage; *tolma* = daring/boldness; "fortitude" captures *tolma*'s steadfast quality better than "courage" or "strength."

---

## Disagreement 6 — 56:3 "partner with the sacred/holy spirit"

- **EMET:** "he chose it as a partner with the sacred spirit"
- **LOGOS:** "he chose it as a partner with the holy spirit"
- **PNEUMA:** "it was chosen as the Spirit's partner"
- **Greek:** *koinōnon tou pneumatos* — partner/companion of the spirit
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he chose it as a partner with the Holy Spirit" (LOGOS). The active "he chose" preserves the master's agency; PNEUMA's passive loses this.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 56:4 "counselors" / advisory role

- **EMET:** "took the son and the trustworthy slaves as counselors"
- **LOGOS:** "took the son and the trustworthy slaves as counselors"
- **PNEUMA:** "called in his son and his reliable slaves as counselors"
- **Note:** All three agree on content.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "He took the son and the trustworthy slaves as counselors" (EMET/LOGOS). "Trustworthy slaves" matches the parable's earlier description.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 56:4 "sacred angels who were first created" vs. "holy angels who were created first"

- **EMET:** "the sacred angels who were first created"
- **LOGOS:** "the holy angels who were created first"
- **PNEUMA:** "the holy angels, the first ones God created"
- **Greek:** *hoi prōtoi ktisthentes angeloi* — the first-created angels
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the holy angels who were created first" (LOGOS). "Created first" is slightly more natural than "first created"; PNEUMA's addition of "God" is accurate but beyond the text.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 56:4 "some place of sojourn" vs. "some resting place"

- **EMET:** "should have some place of sojourn"
- **LOGOS:** "should have some resting place"
- **PNEUMA:** "ought to receive some reward, a place of rest"
- **Greek:** *katoikian tina* — some dwelling place/habitation
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "should have some resting place" (LOGOS). *Katoikia* = dwelling/habitation; "resting place" captures the sense of earned repose; "place of sojourn" (EMET) over-translates with the sojourner motif.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 56:4 "lost the reward of its service" vs. "gone unrewarded"

- **EMET:** "lest it should appear to have lost the reward of its service"
- **LOGOS:** "lest it should appear to have lost the reward of its service"
- **PNEUMA:** "otherwise it would look as if the service it rendered had gone unrewarded"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "lest it should appear to have lost the reward of its service." The appearance of loss (*hina mē doxē*) is legally precise; Hermas argues for fairness in divine accounting.

---

## Disagreement 11 — 56:5 "every flesh in which the sacred/holy spirit has dwelt"

- **EMET:** "every flesh in which the sacred spirit has dwelt"
- **LOGOS:** "every flesh in which the holy spirit has dwelt"
- **PNEUMA:** "every body in which the Holy Spirit has lived"
- **Greek:** *pasa sarx en hē to pneuma to hagion katoikēsei* — every flesh in which the holy spirit dwells/has dwelt
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "every flesh in which the Holy Spirit has dwelt" (LOGOS). "Flesh" (*sarx*) should be preserved — it is a technical term in this pneumatological argument; PNEUMA's "body" softens it.

---

## Disagreement 12 — 56:5 "undefiled and spotless"

- **EMET:** "found undefiled and spotless"
- **LOGOS:** "found undefiled and spotless"
- **PNEUMA:** "found clean and unspotted"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree exactly.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "found undefiled and spotless." This is cultic language (*amiantos kai aspīlos*) from the sacrificial sphere — "undefiled" and "spotless" are the standard terms.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 56.*
